referents.why: 'to them' (autois), masculine plural, is the crowd Pilate asks; the crowd is not among the candidates
referents.category: addressee not offered as a candidate

referents.why: 'What' (ti), neuter interrogative object of 'shall I do': it names no referent, it is what the question asks
'the One' (hon, whom) is the relative pronoun of 'you call ... King of the Jews'; its antecedent is the King (w13), the title of Jesus
referents.category: relative pronoun resolved to its antecedent

referents.why: 'I' (poiēsō, shall I do), first singular in Pilate's question: Pilate is the speaker
referents.category: first person inside speech is the speaker

referents.why: 'you' (legete, you call), second plural in the relative clause: the crowd, Pilate's addressees; not a candidate
referents.category: addressee not offered as a candidate

links.why: the participle 'answering' is the manner of the finite 'was saying'
links.category: participle of answer within finite verb

links.why: the relative clause 'you call' is nested in the question's noun phrase
links.category: relative clause nested in noun phrase

links.why: Object clause of 'was saying': a question. Grammar nesting kept beside the content link.
cl0 is the speech verb 'was saying to them'; cl2 is the question said (R1)

groups.why: the part is the question cl2 alone: the answering participle cl1 is the manner of the frame, not what is said (R1); the addressee is removed because the crowd is not a candidate
groups.category: turn part is the said clause

none_fit.what: Jesus, the referent of 'the One' and of the implied object in this verse, is not offered as a candidate, and neither is the crowd addressed. Both are set to none.

cant_tell.what: the crowd as addressee (slots w6 and cl3s) and so the turn's addressee
cant_tell.why: the crowd is named in Mrk.15.11 (w5) but is not offered as a candidate in this verse
The crowd is the plural addressee but is not in the candidate list.
